extracted.intended_audience: fiction writers (novelists/short-story authors) looking to integrate subplots; intermediate-level creative writers
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on technical methods for inserting and structuring subplots within a main plot—covering POV arrangements, sequencing choices, and how to tie subplots to the central narrative. Focused on practical staging techniques (pendulum, parallel, weaving, sandwich, consecutive) and associated cautions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pendulum Subplot
rubrics_metrics.description: Alternating between two or more points of view (POV) in large sections across a shared narrative: dedicate one chapter to one character’s POV then switch to another, or switch mid-chapter after a scene break so the narrative picks up with another perspective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Typically both narrating characters participate in the same plot points and scenes together, offering competing interpretations or filling in details missing from one perspective through the other. Use clear section/chapter breaks when swapping POV to avoid confusing the reader.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parallel Subplot
rubrics_metrics.description: Alternate between the POVs of two or more characters whose narratives are separate but run alongside one another rather than occurring in the same scenes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Characters rarely interact in the same scenes; their narratives inform each other until they merge when the plot requires. This creates two (or more) strands that later intersect—manage pacing so readers understand the parallel progression and eventual convergence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Weaving
rubrics_metrics.description: Stay in one POV and weave different moments, references, and clues to multiple subplots into the single narrative voice—like coloured reeds in a basket.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Most easily done when each scene furthers more than one plot or character arc; clues, references, and explanations should be woven into scenes organically and naturally. Weaving works best when subplots are closely tied to the main plot and are experienced simultaneously by the main character.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sandwich Subplot
rubrics_metrics.description: Separate out different subplots into distinct chunks placed at different points in the book—for example, one chunk in a prologue and another in an epilogue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Can be used with multiple or single POVs. This technique isolates a subplot from the main body of the narrative, bookending the main story with that subplot’s material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consecutive Subplot
rubrics_metrics.description: Focus first on one set of characters with their subplot and POV until that plotline reaches its end, then shift to a different set of characters and their subplot, eventually bringing the plots together and resolving them as one.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Similar to Parallel Subplots but without alternating back and forth; you 'drop' one plotline entirely while you follow the other. Example: The Two Towers—distinct sections follow different groups before converging. Consider reader continuity when restarting at the beginning of the second plotline.

rubrics_metrics.name: POV-switching clarity / avoid head-hopping
rubrics_metrics.description: When switching narrators or POV, provide a clear visual indication; do not swap POV mid-scene or mid-paragraph.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Head-hopping (unmarked switches of POV within a scene or paragraph) is confusing for readers. Always mark POV changes with chapter/section breaks or other visible cues so the reader can track who is narrating.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tie subplots to the main plot and resolve them satisfactorily
rubrics_metrics.description: Regardless of method chosen, ensure each separate storyline is resolved satisfactorily and—if appropriate—tied together at the end of the novel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subplots should always tie into, support, and expand the main plot. Check that subplots contribute meaningfully to main-plot objectives and that their resolution complements the overall narrative closure.
